description.value: A Funeral for the Living: Objective: stop the first seizure. Challenge the register or shelter the heir; delay brings the carriage to the bridge.
An Invitation in Velvet: Objective: identify the charity's creditor. Examine receipts or interview a recovering patient; delay takes another donor.
The Well that Sings: Objective: find the trapped choir. Follow the pumping chart or answer its verse; delay closes the safe stair.
The Orchard Graves: Objective: preserve tenant testimony. Protect the graves or negotiate an eviction stay; delay scatters the witnesses.
Mirrors at Supper: Objective: establish the debt's original terms. Question the patron or recover a mirror; delay renews a subscription.
An Air Pocket Below: Objective: reach Tom. Send a rope team or restore the bypass; delay extinguishes his lantern.
The Unpaid Foundry: Objective: secure the bell repair. Pay the cast workers or recover withheld wages; delay sets another name ringing.
A Petition with Names: Objective: gather three independent witnesses. Protect public speakers or preserve sealed testimony; delay closes the hearing.
The Missing Verse: Objective: recover the omitted singer. Restore the servants' roll or bargain with the soloist; delay divides the choir.
The Steward's Promise: Objective: settle the binding obligation. Recover the old confession or renegotiate the estate pledge; delay authorizes eviction.
Care Under Threat: Objective: preserve treatment during disclosure. Fund neutral beds or limit the charter transfer; delay abandons patients.
The Last Rope: Objective: evacuate singers. Hold the gate or reduce upper-town water use; delay floods the loft.
At the Carriage Bridge: Objective: stop the final funeral. Present a witnessed release or reshape the bell; delay takes the heir.
The Open Hearing: Objective: end the blood debt. Revoke the subscription or compel confession; delay lets patrons bind a new donor.
The Water Gate: Objective: guarantee safe return. Open the bypass or settle a shared reservoir duty; delay traps the rescue crew.
A Quiet Inheritance: Objective: decide estate governance. Protect tenant housing or establish a wage trust; record who holds the promise.
Charity after Midnight: Objective: choose honest care. Transfer the charter or establish patient oversight; record whose debts remain.
A Parish Remembered: Objective: decide how remembrance survives. Publish the complete roll or appoint custodians; record who maintains the safe water route.
Living Funeral: the carriage announces an heir's burial before sunset.
Charity Invitation: the crew is offered care in exchange for unnamed signatures.
Water Hymn: the town's wells repeat a singer's plea for a rope.
Register Addition: another tenant's name appears beneath the living heir.
Patient Recovery: a patient wakes younger while a donor disappears.
Pump Halt: a frightened warden stops the only safe diving interval.
Orchard Eviction: bailiffs bring a seal issued before the previous heir died.
Mirror Accusation: a reflection reveals someone in the ballroom as a creditor.
Loft Signal: Tom lights a lamp below the reservoir's surface.
Wage Demand: the bellfounders refuse a repair that repeats the old exploitation.
Witness Offer: a petitioner agrees to speak if private records stay sealed.
Bypass Leak: engineers ask the crew to choose which neighborhood loses water.
Carriage Crossing: the horses approach the bridge carrying an empty coffin.
Contract Amendment: the broker offers a smaller debt that still binds an innocent family.
Choir Dispute: two surviving rolls disagree about a servant's name.
Estate Confession: the steward admits wages were withheld to protect the heirs.
Charter Threat: the patrons threaten to close care before the hearing begins.
Rope Break: a diver needs aid while the choir's last air pocket shrinks.
Foundry Opening: the hot bell can be reshaped during one public witness window.
Third Witness: a patient will testify if treatment remains guaranteed.
Sluice Arrival: the final pump interval reveals the old water gate.
Tenant Council: families decide whether to accept joint responsibility for repairs.
Public Procession: the court moves to bury the petition under a grand ceremony.
Nameless Verse: the choir refuses evacuation until the omitted servant is remembered.
Paid Promise: the carriage waits for proof that wages reached the living families.
Care Without Debt: an honest fund offers limited beds and transparent obligations.
Water Returned: the upper town sees the cost of the reservoir agreement.
Quiet Bell: a new toll reflects the crew's settlement of the funeral promise.
Open Charter: the court's confession changes who governs charitable care.
Remembered Parish: the final hymn names those the town chose to preserve.
